extracted.intended_audience: Project Gutenberg volunteers/transcribers, eBook editors, and distributors/readers of this edition of Pudd'nhead Wilson
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and production notes for transcribing, emending, presenting, and legally distributing the Project Gutenberg edition of Mark Twain's Pudd'nhead Wilson (1894/1899 comparison), plus the Project Gutenberg license terms governing distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialect transcription rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The soliloquies and conversations in the novel follow some general rules. Twain introduced some variations in the spelling of dialect, and sometimes the sound of dialect, but the end meaning seems to be the same thing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a mapping of standard spellings to dialect variants and be consistent; the Project Gutenberg transcription supplies a table (e.g., and → en; against → agin/ag'in/ag'in'; because → 'ca'se; going → gwine/gwyne; that → dat; the → de; then → den; there → dere/dah; these → dese; they → dey/deh; this → dis; was → 'uz; with → wid; where → whah). Document any departures from original spellings and explain rationale in Detailed Notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base edition selection
rubrics_metrics.description: This version is based on the 1894 publication of this novel in Hartford. This was Twain's original American release of the novel in book form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the edition used as the transcription base (here: 1894 Hartford). When making emendations, check later authorized editions (e.g., 1899 Harper & Brothers) and note where changes align with or differ from those editions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emendation policy and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Emendations were made in some spots; these emendations were checked with the 1899 version of Pudd'nhead Wilson published by Harper & Brothers. A few emendations were made that were not authorized by Twain in 1899; these are noted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only make emendations where justified (typographical errors, obvious errata, or supported by authoritative later edition). Record every emendation in Detailed Notes, explain reasoning, and indicate whether the change appears in later authorized editions. Provide inline markers or hoverable annotations in the HTML to reveal original text where emendations occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyphenation and line-break handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Many words are split between two lines for spacing purposes in the original text. These words are hyphenated in the physical book, but there is a question sometimes as to whether the hyphen should be retained in transcription.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resolve line-break hyphenation by consulting authoritative later editions: remove spurious hyphens inserted for line breaks (e.g., transcribe 'barber shop' rather than 'barber-shop' when original hyphen appears only due to line wrap) unless later edition preserves hyphen. Document each decision in Detailed Notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct obvious typographical errors and misspellings
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the original contains obvious errors (missing words, misspellings, misplaced punctuation), correct them when verifiable and record the change (examples include inserting missing 'it', changing 'dicision' to 'decision', etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make corrections when the intended reading is clear and cross-check against later editions. List each correction in Detailed Notes with page/chapter references and explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency in dialect renderings
rubrics_metrics.description: Twain introduced variant spellings within the text (e.g., dey vs. deh); the transcription notes such inconsistencies and treats isolated deviations as likely errata when supported by context or later edition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for internal consistency in rendering dialect, but preserve intentional variation when authorial. When a token appears inconsistent and later editions correct it, document the change as an assumed erratum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention of chapter titles for indexing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chapter Titles, such as Doom in Chapter XXI., were not part of Twain's book. They remain from another version of this book. The chapter titles are used in PG's Mark Twain index, so we have retained them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retain non-original chapter titles when necessary for Project Gutenberg indexing or cross-references, and explicitly note that they were not part of the original book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement of the Author's Note
rubrics_metrics.description: The Author's Note to Those Extraordinary Twins is actually the author's introduction to the novella, Those Extraordinary Twins. Twain originally produced this book with two parts: Pudd'nhead Wilson and Those Extraordinary Twins. Project Gutenberg offers both stories, so we present the Author's Note as the Introduction to Those Extraordinary Twins, as Twain intended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow authorial intent for placement of front-matter when possible; if the material spans multiple works, place notes where the author intended and provide cross-links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide access to original and emended text (HTML annotations)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the HTML version of this e-book, you can place your cursor over the faint silver dotted lines below the changed text to discover the original text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When emendations are made, include inline HTML annotations, hover-text, or footnotes that allow readers to view the original wording. Ensure readers can discover original text and the nature of emendations easily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record detailed editorial notes by chapter
rubrics_metrics.description: The Detailed Notes Section includes issues that have come up during transcription and itemizes reasons behind certain editorial decisions (e.g., whether to retain or change hyphenation, punctuation fixes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a Detailed Notes section listing per-chapter corrections, hyphenation decisions, and other transcription issues, with page references and rationale.
